transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-10 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lavender Head of MLOps), Ethan Ross (CTO), Samir Patel (SRE)
---
Auto-summary (may be rough): Week 3 POC lab audit. We went through three test runs versus their current vendor, focused on p95 and p99 tail latency under mixed QPS, plus throughput under sustained load. Discussed caching and fallback playbook.
---
00:00 Alex Monroe: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, we wanted to run the audit results and decide next steps for the fallback dispatch test.
00:22 Maya Chen: thanks Alex, we only have about 45 min, we've got a spike test planned tomorrow so want to confirm changes.
00:31 Priya Singh: great, I'll start with the numbers i pulled from the lab. quick note: some of the labels in the CSV got munged, so bear with me if a couple model names show up weird.
00:45 Priya Singh: run 1, baseline (their incumbent) p95 was 310ms, p99 820ms at 60 qps with our standard prompts. Redwood run at same config p95 220ms, p99 540ms. throughput sustained tokens/sec about 14k vs baseline 9.5k.
01:12 Ethan Ross: interesting, those are median-ish improvements but i'd like to understand tail behavior under burst. our app is bursty.
01:23 Priya Singh: yes, we did a burst test — at 95% load the baseline p99 jumped to ~1.4s, while Redwood's p99 was ~780ms, so still better but tail widens for both. we also saw more consistent kv-cache hit ratio on our side, ~72% vs incumbent 45%.
01:47 Samir Patel: when you say kv-cache hit, was that prefix caching or full-session cache? we do a lot of few-shot so prefix matters.
01:56 Priya Singh: prefix caching mostly, we tuned the policy to preserve recent tokens for interactive flows. that helped reduce recompute on the first token of the second turn.
02:10 Alex Monroe: one area we noted was batching — the baseline was batching more aggressively which helped throughput but spiked latency; we proposed a dynamic batching policy that trades a small latency bump for throughput gains when the 95th is under target.
02:32 Maya Chen: what's the delta on cost there? our finance team will ask.
02:36 Alex Monroe: rough numbers in the deck, but for the dynamic batch config it reduces token compute cost about 12-17% at our current load; worst-case p95 goes up by ~40ms.
02:50 Ethan Ross: can you share the math and the test harness? reproducibility was a pain last time with their vendor.
03:00 Priya Singh: yes, we will share the harness and sanitized logs. note: some of the sample traces have redacted ids so the timing jitter looks odd but i flagged those.
03:15 Priya Singh: we also tested int8 quantization variant. it reduced memory footprint and increased peak throughput ~20% but added about 60-80ms to p99 in worst-case workloads. for many of your flow types quant is reasonable, but for strict latency endpoints we recommended non-quantized or a mixed fleet.
03:40 Ethan Ross: mixed fleet meaning we route critical endpoints to non-quantized and background jobs to quantized?
03:45 Priya Singh: exactly. Redwood routing policies can steer by route tag, latency SLO, or cost tier. in lab we set a fallback so if latency exceeds the threshold it re-routes to a hot non-quantized slot.
04:00 Samir Patel: curious about fallback time — is there a cold start when switching variants?
04:08 Priya Singh: good question. we pre-warm hot slots for critical routes; fallback switch is usually <150ms extra overhead because we maintain warmed KV caches for hot variants. if the fallback spins a new instance there's an additional warmup, which is why we suggested a dedicated slot for your critical endpoints.
04:32 Maya Chen: dedicated slot trial would help us quantify that. how long to spin one up?
04:36 Alex Monroe: we can stand up a trial slot in the dedicated pool within 24 hours for your region, typically we suggest a 1-week stress window.
04:45 Maya Chen: perfect.
04:50 Ethan Ross: i want to call out security — do we have clear KMS integration docs and audit log granularity? we need per-request audit for compliance.
05:00 Alex Monroe: yes, Priya will share the SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes. audit logs include token-level request IDs, routing decisions, and per-request latency. our private deployment option gives customer-managed KMS if you need.
05:18 Priya Singh: adding — for Private/VPC you can have HSM-backed key management, and we keep an audit trail with 90-day retention by default; we can extend retention for enterprise plans.
05:32 Samir Patel: ok, we'll need 1) SOC2 + KMS doc, 2) sample audit log schema, 3) sample anonymized traces by Friday.
05:43 Alex Monroe: action: i'll send security bundle and the simplified CSV of results.
05:48 Priya Singh: about the routing playbook — we recommended a threshold of 350ms for p95 to trigger fallback to non-quantized variant; for your workload that gets us below the incumbent's typical p95 in most runs.
06:08 Maya Chen: is that threshold adjustable on the fly? we might tweak during the trial.
06:12 Priya Singh: yes adjustable; the console exposes live threshold toggles and we can commit rollbacks.
06:20 Ethan Ross: what about model compatibility — if we fallback to a different model family, does output divergence risk our QA pipeline?
06:30 Priya Singh: think of it as model varianting: same base model but different quantization/optimizations. output divergence was minimal in our evals— top-level semantics were preserved, but you might see slight tokenization differences in third decimal. we can attach regen tests to catch any regressions.
06:52 Samir Patel: can we see a quick side-by-side sample of 10 prompts comparing tokens and latency?
06:58 Priya Singh: yes, we'll include a 10-prompt side-by-side with deltas in the CSV.
07:05 Alex Monroe: recap then: Redwood to provide harness and sanitized logs, dedicated slot trial sizing and cost, security bundle and SOC2/KMS notes, and a 10-prompt side-by-side. Lavender to upload representative prompt set and confirm trial window.
07:22 Maya Chen: correct. also we'll run our own heavy spike at 95% tomorrow to validate fallback.
07:30 Ethan Ross: timeline — can we aim to start the dedicated trial Monday 2027-02-14?
07:36 Alex Monroe: yes we can provision by Monday morning if we get the prompt set by Sunday EOD.
07:43 Priya Singh: note: there were two noisy traces in run 2 i want to flag — network jitter on the run VM, that's why p99 jumped at 18:40 mark. we can re-run that sequence.
07:58 Samir Patel: we'll re-run too, we'll correlate with our infra logs and share.
08:05 Alex Monroe: any other open risks?
08:09 Maya Chen: only the finance question — need cost delta and guardrails for the dynamic batching config, but that's secondary to validating latency.
08:18 Alex Monroe: we'll include cost delta in the mail.
08:22 Ethan Ross: perfect, thanks.
08:26 Alex Monroe: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the package and set up the trial.
08:32 Meeting ended.
